title: Scale ramp troubleshooting journal
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad capturing commands, outputs, timings and hypotheses for the dedicated GPU pool scaling thrash / long warmup incident that started showing up intermittently in Dec->Feb. Goal is to preserve what I ran and why, so we can reproduce or handoff.

Top-level summary (short):
- Symptom: repeated scale-up followed by aggressive scale-down within 60–90s for low-medium steady traffic bursts; resulting cold-started pods struggle to reach steady throughput for ~90–180s, causing higher 99th latency and client retries.
- Observed during canary for dedicated pool A (eu-west-1) and sporadically in dedicated B.
- Suspected contributors: too-short scale-down cooldowns, node reclaim ordering, model weight lazy-load + large KV cache fill time, and autoscaler reacting to short spike artifacts (health-check retry noise).

Timeline / commands run (notes):
2025-12-04 09:12 — initial reproduce attempt on staging-dedicated-A
- Start synthetic steady load: wrk/hey to /v1/generate endpoint sending 2 RPS (1-2 token avg).
  - hey -z 10m -q 2 -c 2 http://staging-dedicated-a.internal/v1/generate
- Observe autoscaler logs on controller host:
  - kubectl logs -n infra deploy/redwood-autoscaler --since=3m | tail -n 200
  - snippet: "scale_decision: replicas=2->6; reason=metric:request_rate spike(1m avg)"
  - then 70s later: "scale_decision: replicas=6->2; reason=metric:request_rate drop(30s avg)"
- Pod events: kubectl describe hpa redwood-serving-hpa -n serving -> saw target reached then ephemeral drop.

2025-12-04 09:20 — verify pod startup times
- kubectl get pods -n serving -l app=model-serving -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,AGE:.metadata.creationTimestamp,STATUS:.status.phase,READY:.status.containerStatuses[0].ready -w
- Observed pod Ready==true at ~40–55s, but application-level readiness (model loaded & responding) only after ~120–160s (application readinessProbe is HTTP /health returns 200 earlier but model not warmed).
- Grepped logs from model-container:
  - kubectl logs pod/<pod> -n serving -c model | grep "weights loaded" -n
  - sample output: "[00:01:40] weights loaded from S3, kv-cache init start"

2026-01-14 15:02 — experiment: bump scale-down cooldown and minReplicas
- Edit HPA/Autoscaler config to set cooldown to 180s and minReplicas from 2->4 temporarily.
  - kubectl patch hpa redwood-serving-hpa -n serving --type merge -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":180}}}}'
- Result: thrash frequency dropped, but cost/replica increased (expected). Initial client 99th latency improved during 2–10 RPS steady bursts.

Error snippets seen in infra logs:
- autoscaler: "failed to fetch pod metrics: metrics-server not ready" (transient; correlated with scale decisions at t+2m)
- kubelet: "eviction: reclaiming GPU resources" (when node scale-down started while pods not fully drained)
- model-container: "kv-cache hydration timeout after 45s, falling back to partial cache"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Autoscaler uses too-short sampling windows for scale-down; a transient 30s dip flips it. Should use longer stabilizationWindow / cooldown to accommodate model warmup.
2) ReadinessProbe only checks liveness/basic HTTP - not model-ready; so HPA sees pods as ready earlier and traffic is routed while model still warming. We need a model-ready probe (or add delayed routing via negative weight to LB until model-ready).
3) Node reclamation order: cloud autoscaler sometimes evicts nodes with newest model pods (due to binpack heuristics), causing more concurrent cold starts. Prefer graceful drain ordering that favors keeping warm nodes.
4) KV cache fill time: initial requests do heavy S3 pulls; combined with throttled bandwidth this can make first 30–90s unusable. Consider prefetch or background warmers on scale-up.
5) Metrics noise: short health-check flaps or scrape timeouts are being interpreted as traffic drops. We should smooth request_rate metric (p95 window) used by decision logic.

Commands / checks to reproduce / capture more data: (copy when doing next run)
- tail autoscaler decisions: kubectl logs -n infra deploy/redwood-autoscaler --since=10m | sed -n '1,400p' > ~/tmp/autoscaler.log
- scrape prometheus range around event: curl -g 'http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query_range?query=redwood_gpu_pool_utilization&start=...&end=...&step=15s'
- pod startup waterfall: kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' -n serving | grep -E "Scheduled|Pulling|Started|Ready"
- collect container logs for first 5 pods after scale-up: for p in $(kubectl get pods -n serving -l app=model-serving -o name | head -n 5); do kubectl logs $p -n serving -c model > /tmp/${p##*/}.log; done

Recent experiments and notes: 
- 2026-02-02: added "model_ready" readiness endpoint that returns 200 only after KV cache filled to 50% or explicit 'warm' state. Result: client errors dropped, but autoscaler still scaled down before steady-state due to short lookback.
- 2026-02-15: added a light-weight background prefetcher (warm-worker) that triggers on scale-up; reduces cold warm time from avg 140s -> 55s, but more bursty network IO during warm.
- 2026-02-27: toggled cloud node-pool scale-down delay (GCP) to 300s to test node reclaim ordering — fewer evictions of warm nodes, but longer idle cost.

Observed metrics (excerpt):
- warm_time_before_prefetch: median 140s, p95 220s
- warm_time_after_prefetch: median 55s, p95 120s
- average per-pod first-5-requests latency: 2.1s -> 0.9s after warm-worker
- autoscaler decisions: typical pattern -> up 4 replicas within 20s, down 4 replicas after 65–75s.

Small experiments to run next (ranked):
1) Flip autoscaler scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds to 240s in canary and monitor 3-day window. Hypothesis: thrash stops; cost delta measurable.
2) Make HPA rely on smoothed request_rate (60s exponential window) instead of instantaneous; simulate repeated daisychained dips in load to validate.
3) Push warm-worker into production behind feature flag that only runs when pool replicas<8 and predicted scale-up (fast path). Observe network egress impact.
4) Add metric "model_ready_ratio" exported by pods (0..1) and feed it into autoscaler as a soft signal so it avoids scaling down if many pods are model_ready==false.
5) Revisit node-eviction order in cloud autoscaler integration (prefer nodes with >60% GPU-util or nodes with pinned models).

Notes to self (operational checklists):
- When reproducing, always capture: autoscaler.log, prometheus query window, pod logs, node events, cloud autoscaler events (GCP: gcloud compute instance-group-managers list-instances --region=...), and the LB health-check logs.
- Annotate any pod that was evicted with reason: kubectl describe node <node> | grep -A5 "Non-terminated Pods" + check "Evicted" events.

Quick ideas (low-effort):
- Make readinessProbe check a small in-memory flag set only when kv-cache reaches N keys; reduces false-ready routing.
- Add a short hold-off annotation on pods created by redwood-autoscaler to prevent immediate node-level scaleDown decisions for X seconds.

Longer term / product improvements:
- Expose "warm_start" SLO to customers / internal dashboards; give per-route warm probabilities and expected latency curves.
- Autoscaler should support composite signal: request_rate + model_ready_fraction + node_gpu_utilization.
- Allow reserved warm slots (minReplicas by region) with cheaper standby instances (lower-cost VM class) to reduce cost of keeping warm capacity.

Decisions made so far:
- temp: bumped scaleDown stabilizationWindowSeconds to 180s on canary (2026-01-14). Will revert if cost unacceptable after 14 days.
- implemented model_ready probe (2026-02-02) and warm-worker (2026-02-15) in staging; both behind flags.

Open questions / unresolved: 
- Is there an interaction with the global routing layer that pushes traffic to new pods ahead of readinessProbe updates? Check API Gateway config and per-route weights.
- Cache-priming bandwidth: can S3 concurrency be increased for prefetch without impacting other customers? Need infra cost estimate.
- Are any other services (e.g., metric exporter) causing artefactual dips in the request_rate metric? Need to audit scrape intervals and missing scrape fallbacks.

Next actions (next 7 days):
- Run canary with scaleDown window=240s for 72 hours. Collect cost delta and 99th latency. (Owner: me)
- Add model_ready_ratio metric to prometheus (Owner: Priya) and wire a test autoscaler policy that factors it in (Owner: Diego)
- Create runbook snippet for on-call to increase scaleDown window quickly in case of production-wide thrash (Owner: me).

Random notes / breadcrumbs I want to remember: 
- Observed odd timestamp mismatch once: model logs show "weights loaded at 00:01:40" but pod creation time suggests longer — double-check container timezone/logging.
- Some pods logged warnings about CUDA driver minor version mismatch but still started; could degrade perf during warm. File: /var/log/nvidia-installer.log
- Revisit placement groups: collocating warm pods can reduce repeated node-scale events.

If handing off, essentials to capture for next person:
- Reproduction command (hey/wrk, endpoints), autoscaler logs (give exact cut times), prometheus queries used, and the patch to HPA used. Keep note of cost impact and revert plan.

-- end of scratchpad (will iteratively update)
